To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a recently introduced flame model, based on the concept of a flamelet, is used to determine the mass-burning rate of premixed laminar flames; (2) integral analysis is used to obtain the results; (3) the results can be used in experiments and numerical studies of premixed flames; and (4) the mass-burning-rate expression is based on the burned edge of the flamelet, not on the stoichiometric edge.

(1) the integral analysis of a recently introduced flame-sheet model yields new expressions for the mass-burning rate of a premixed stretched flame that (2) reduce to the same expressions found earlier with asymptotics techniques for Lewis numbers near unity but (3) differ from the latter for Lewis numbers far from unity.
the mass burning rate can be expressed as a function of the mass flux of the unburned reactants and the stretch rate of the flamelet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a more general and rigorous analysis of the mass burning rate for premixed, stretched flames.
a new approach to the mass burning rate, which is based on integral analysis of a recently introduced flame model.
the mass burning rate of stretched flames.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for stretched flames, asymptotic techniques should be used to determine mass burning rates and integral analysis should be used to derive the flamelet model.
integral analysis and large-activation-energy techniques are equally appropriate to determine the burning rate of stretched flames.
both approaches are valid and give the same results for Lewis numbers close and above unity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the integral analysis provides a very useful tool for the analysis of stretched flamelets.

the mass burning rate of a stretched flame, based on the flamelet model, can be determined from a simple expression that reduces to the large-activation-energy results for Lewis numbers close or equal to 1.
the integral analysis of stretched premixed flames is a powerful tool to obtain new expressions for the mass-burning rate and the mass flux of species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mass burning rate of stretched premixed flames can be determined by measuring the mass burning rate and the stretch rate at the flamelet edge.
the mass burning rate is a function of the mass fraction of the product species, the mass flux of the reactant species, and a length scale, which is the distance between the fresh and burned edge.
the burned edge is the appropriate boundary condition for stretched flames in the context of large-activation-energy theory.
